subject: using mirt's plot-method in a separate function

messages.author: 1c8e58baceb6e062
messages.subject: using mirt's plot-method in a separate function
parts:
Hey all,
I am trying to incorporate mirt into a new package I am building. However, I am getting hung up on one issue: I cannot use the plot-method from mirt. Even when the package is listed as a dependency, R assumes that I want plot.default. I am at a loss, thought I am hoping I just missed something obvious. Does anyone have any suggestions?
Thanks,
Isaac

messages.author: 1c8e58baceb6e062
messages.subject: Re: using mirt's plot-method in a separate function
parts:
Yes, sorry.

In my normal day to day use, when I attach mirt

library(mirt)

I can use

plot(my_model, type = "trace")

I would like to do the same in my package. I thought that I could list mirt as a dependency and then use

mirt::plot(my_model, type = 'trace').

When I do this, I get

Error: 'plot' is not an exported object from 'namespace:mirt'

I get the same error when I try

import::from(mirt, 'plot')

I cannot think of another way to try this. I even tried it without first attaching the package, but I get this error:

Error in as.double(y) :
  cannot coerce type 'S4' to vector of type 'double'


I am afraid I don't know any other way to direct R to the plot method found in mirt.

Thank you for considering my question.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: using mirt's plot-method in a separate function
parts:
If you add mirt as a Depends: package in your DESCRIPTION file then this should resolve your issue in the easiest way since this will also import the S4 plotting methods and dependencies. Though you'll have to manage any naming conflict in your package. HTH.

Phil
